key_insight: Laser breakdown inside a water droplet generates an internal plasma pressure load that drives liquid-shell expansion and breakup, while the emitted shock wave is strongly affected by ambient pressure.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and control droplet atomization and shock emission in laser-based spray, microfluidic, and laser-processing applications.
method: Nanosecond laser-induced breakdown was performed inside micrometer-sized water droplets in the finite-beam regime (D0/Db≈2).
Simultaneous imaging of droplet deformation and shock-wave propagation was used to separate liquid and gas-phase dynamics.
Experiments were repeated over a range of ambient pressures and laser energies to compare low-energy bubble-driven deformation with high-energy shell ablation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simultaneous quantitative measurements showing that shock propagation changes substantially with ambient pressure, while droplet morphology and expansion remain nearly unchanged under the same internal plasma-driven load.
watch_item: The mechanism is established for a specific droplet size and finite-beam focusing condition, so extrapolation to other droplet sizes, beam geometries, or liquids should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Ambient-pressure effects on shock emission and liquid-shell expansion following optical breakdown inside water droplets
